purpose: DP-5's named prerequisite: confirm the HC mix epilogue feeds the most dense consumers before the F16 write is moved into it. Census of the single F16 staging-cast kernel and of its producers and consumers.
layer_scope: layers 16-47 (32 layers) for the hc_*_down roles - the promoted 16-47 scope
verdict: CONFIRMED: the HC down projections are 64.0% of the cast total, the largest single block, so moving the F16 write into the HC mix epilogue first is the right order.
recoverable_estimate_note: SUPERSEDED by bandwidth_measurement: the whole-row 87.3 ms is an over-estimate; the defensible target is the HC pair at 55.9 ms (0.36%).
limits: One model, one quant, one host (gfx1151), one case (code-p4096), one window, one profile, prefill only. Per-role-per-kernel join inside a marked window; diagnostic, not a wall measurement.

bandwidth_measurement.method: Raw rocprofv3 kernel trace filtered to the qwen4exp_prefill_p4096_ marker window; elements = Grid_Size_X*Y*Z as WORK-ITEMS (section 8 rule 2), NOT multiplied by Workgroup_Size_X. Reproduces the artifact's 1056 launches / 131.001 ms exactly.
bandwidth_measurement.byte_model: read F32 (4 B) + write F16 (2 B) = 6 B per element
bandwidth_measurement.finding: The cast's apparent bandwidth RISES as the transfer shrinks, from 192.1 GB/s at 10,485,760 elements per launch to 595.4 GB/s at 655,360 - and the total of 229.0 GB/s is 103.6% of the DRAM roof, which is impossible for pure DRAM traffic. So the small roles are partly L2-served and their 6 B/element model is NOT a DRAM model.
bandwidth_measurement.defensible_target: The hc_*_down pair alone: 16.106 GB at 192.1 GB/s = 86.9% of roof, the largest transfers and the only ones plausibly DRAM-bound. Net saving 4/6 x 83.861 = 55.9 ms = 0.36% of the union.
bandwidth_measurement.refuted: The whole-row 4/6 x 131.001 = 87.3 ms figure is an OVER-ESTIMATE: it applies a DRAM byte model to roles whose apparent bandwidth is above the DRAM roof, i.e. whose traffic is partly served by cache and would not be saved by eliminating the kernel.
